points.description: Lower bound: proves James cannot guarantee reaching the last row with at most 2 penalties (i.e. n ≥ 3), by describing a placement/adversary argument for Peter that forces at least 2 penalties against any James strategy.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only proves that at least 1 penalty can be forced, or gives an incomplete adversary argument for 2 penalties.

points.description: Upper bound, case where the selected cell in the second row is not at the edge column: gives a valid James strategy that reaches the last row with at most 2 penalties, using the one-per-row and at-most-one-per-column rules, with justification.
Upper bound, case where the selected cell in the second row is on the edge (e.g. first or last column): gives a valid strategy and justification that at most 2 penalties are received.

rubric.notes: Equivalent strategies and wording earn marks. Full marks need answer 3, a lower-bound proof and a complete upper-bound strategy covering both edge and non-edge cases. Minor non-negligible errors in an otherwise complete solution lose part of a point.
